test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 13 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are given followed by three conclusions. Consider the statements and conclusions as true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, and then find out which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements?

**statement :**

1. Some nails are rings.</font

options.text: Only conclusion I and II follow

solution:
statement :

1. Some nails are rings.

2. All rings are fingers.

3. All nails are bracelets.

The least possible Venn diagram is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44b2c39720ccf43295ce3d134509bae3c5f09c687f541cd800fe06834b6f4102.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6b812cb0eeb9516851e763daf346bf5f8a0d85bc217d8634bdef56b0d0020999.png] 

conclusion :

(I) Some bracelets are rings. - **True **(Because Some nails are rings and All nails are bracelets so, Some bracelets are also rings)

(II) Some fingers are nails. - **True **(Because Some nails are rings and All rings are fingers so, Some fingers are also nails)

(III) No ring is a bracelet. - **False **((Because Some nails are rings and All nails are bracelets so, Some rings are bracelets)

So, Only conclusion I and II follow.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusion I and II follow".**
